name: Tephi

attributes.attribute: one of the builders of the ramparts at Tara
marked the Rampart of Tephi with staff and brooch

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Tephi is an Irish heroine from the place-poetry called the Dindshenchas. The Dindshenchas recount how early builders made the ramparts at the royal hill of Tara. Tephi appears in that account as one of those builders. The source calls her the daughter of an Egyptian pharaoh. It also calls her a fierce warrior. A little-known champion carried her away. His name was Camson. With her staff and her brooch, Tephi traced the outline of the great earthen walls at Tara. People called those walls the Rampart of Tephi. She died in Ireland. The tale does not place her grave there. Some texts say it may lie in Spain. The story may reflect how Macha built the capital of Ulster. In that tale Macha traced the raths with the pin of her brooch. Or the Tephi story may have inspired the Macha tale. The record does not say which came first.

okr.objective: Record Tephi as an Irish heroine from the Dindshenchas place-poetry.
key_results: Names Tephi among the early builders of the ramparts at Tara
